title: Art & Forgery
subtitle: Learn to look like a curator, think like a forger and test like a conservation scientist — from your first close look at a painting to a full authentication dossier.
summary: Start from zero: how to look at a painting, what it is physically made of, and how styles and materials changed over five centuries. Then meet the forgers — from Michelangelo's buried Cupid to Van Meegeren, Beltracchi and the Knoedler scandal — and learn every tool used to catch them: connoisseurship, provenance research, ultraviolet, infrared and X-ray imaging, pigment dating, tree rings and bomb-peak radiocarbon. Labs run real methods on real data (the 1950–2019 carbon-14 curve, published sapwood statistics), and the course ends with your own authentication dossier on a case file. Every fact is sourced and dated; disputed attributions and AI claims are marked as disputed.
outcomes: Describe and analyse a painting in the vocabulary of an expert — line, colour, technique, the artist's hand — and place it in its period.
Explain how a painting is built, layer by layer, and when key pigments, supports and binders became available.
Tell the stories of the major forgers and name the weakness each one exploited: the eye, the paper trail, the lab or the market.
Interpret ultraviolet, infrared and X-ray images, set a terminus post quem from pigment analysis, date an oak panel by its rings and read a bomb-peak radiocarbon result.
Audit a chain of ownership for gaps and red flags, including the 1933–1945 period.
Weigh connoisseurship, science and documents into a reasoned authentication opinion — and read an 'AI says it's genuine' headline critically.
prerequisites: None — the course starts from zero.
Helpful: access to an online museum collection to choose paintings for your looking journal.

outputs.title: Looking journal
outputs.description: Close descriptions of real paintings you chose, written the way a curator looks: what is there, how it was made, what a forger would find hardest to copy.

outputs.title: Examiner's casebook
outputs.description: Your red-flag checklist and the saved results of the provenance, imaging, pigment, tree-ring and radiocarbon labs, each with a note on what it does and doesn't prove.

outputs.title: Headline audit
outputs.description: A short audit of one real authentication headline — an AI attribution or a 'lost masterpiece' — separating the claim, the evidence, the dispute and what would settle it.

outputs.title: Authentication dossier
outputs.description: A sourced opinion on the case-file portrait, as an examiner would write it for a museum: the evidence from every method, how much each weighs, your verdict with a stated confidence, and what to do next.
